newsitem.title: USA: N.J. says unemployment rate drops to six-year low.
newsitem.headline: N.J. says unemployment rate drops to six-year low.

text.p: New Jersey's unemployment rated dropped to 5.9 percent in January, falling below six percent for the first time since December 1990, the state's Labor Department said.
The January rate was an improvement from the prior month's 6.1 percent rate, the department said.
Preliminary figures for the month show the number of people working in New Jersey in January rose 9,600 from December to a seasonally adjusted level of 3.7 million.

"The relatively good weather in January and our continuing economic growth helped bring us good news this month," Labor Commissioner Mel Gelade said in a statement. "New Jersey has had a net increase of 168,600 more jobs since January 1994."
Employment growth from December to January was highest in the services sector, which rose by 4,900. Manufacturing employment rose by 3,200 to 486,500.
